title: Joe Biden’s cancer has spread, Hunter Biden says
description: In a BBC interview, Hunter Biden also acknowledged that the pardon he received from his father was “not fair” or good for the country.

title: GOP-controlled Senate delivers win for Trump with Blanche confirmation
description: The Senate narrowly confirmed former Trump personal attorney Todd Blanche as U.S. Attorney General, a major win for the president's approach to keeping the Justice Department close to the White House.

title: Senate narrowly approves Todd Blanche as AG, capping tough confirmation fight
description: The early-morning 50-49 vote grants President Donald Trump’s former criminal defense lawyer a full stint as the head of the Justice Department, which has been rocked by vacancies and controversies.

title: Pirro, Trump’s longtime champion, is on the outs over Reflecting Pool move
description: D.C.’s top prosecutor spent a year navigating the president’s demands. Now she finds her job at risk amid a rare break with him over cases of alleged vandalism.

title: Longtime San Francisco nonprofit will close as city gets tougher on crime
description: The demise of SF Pretrial, which for 50 years has provided diversion services, came after the mayor cut its budget and as Democrats’ attitudes toward crime shift.

title: Voter turnout surges in Tennessee after Black-majority district is erased
description: High Democratic turnout for House primaries in Shelby County, which includes Memphis, is the latest sign that redistricting may be energizing Black Southern voters.

title: Democratic voters who used to back Susan Collins aren’t so sure anymore
description: Sen. Susan Collins (R-Maine) has counted on split-ticket voters to help her win office in a blue state. Some of those supporters are more reluctant to vote for her again.

title: Minnesota GOP divided over Mike Lindell's potential gubernatorial nomination
description: Mike Lindell of "MyPillow" fame, might win the GOP primary for Minnesota governor running on a Trump platform. Other Republicans are concerned that his closeness could hurt his chances in November.

title: Legal scholar Lawrence Lessig on how a Maine law could topple Super PACs
description: NPR's Scott Simon speaks with legal scholar and activist Lawrence Lessig about the influence of outside money in elections and a court challenge to a Maine state law capping donations to Super PACs.

title: Week in Politics: Blanche confirmed as attorney general; Iran-Oman Strait deal stalls
description: We look at what it took to get Todd Blanche confirmed as U.S. attorney general, as well as the proposed deal between Iran and Oman to control the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Private prisons announce $1.4 billion in revenue as immigration detentions climb
description: That revenue does not include net proceeds of $1.6 billion made by CoreCivic after the recent sale of four of their facilities to the Department of Homeland Security.

title: Data centers are a political issue crossing party lines, driving voters to candidates
description: Wisconsin Democratic candidate for governor Francesca Hong called for a moratorium on data centers. So did Ohio Republican governor hopeful Vivek Ramaswamy, as data centers begin to dominate campaigns.

title: Senate votes to confirm Todd Blanche as attorney general
description: The Senate confirmed Blanche by a 50-49 vote early Saturday morning, elevating President Trump's former personal lawyer to head the Justice Department.

title: Why a prosecution of Anthony Fauci could face challenges in court
description: The Justice Department faces numerous pressures and challenges as it decides whether to prosecute Anthony Fauci following a Senate committee's contempt referral.

title: Trump says he’ll bring ballroom fight to Supreme Court after lower court halts work
description: An appeals court ruled earlier Friday that construction must stop until Congress authorizes the project. The ballroom is among the president’s top priorities for this term.

title: Cassidy backs Blanche for attorney general, appearing to clear way for confirmation
description: The Senate could hold the final vote on President Donald Trump’s pick to lead the Justice Department as soon as Friday.

title: Trump won’t let the Supreme Court have the last word
description: The president moved this week to counter legal defeats on ending birthright citizenship and firing a Fed governor, while seeking the justices’ help with his ballroom.

title: Court deals setback to Trump’s war on wind as Pentagon is ordered to review projects
description: The Defense Department stopped processing national security reviews of wind projects in May, despite a law demanding they be completed in 75 days.

title: What happened under Trump this week
description: The administration approved a new flu shot but is raising fresh questions about the relationship between autism and other vaccines.

title: One chart shows the backlash to gutting the Voting Rights Act
description: Democratic turnout for House primaries in Shelby County, Tennessee, a majority-Black county, surged to the highest level in a decade.

title: Women in Maine may choose the victor in this year's Senate race
description: The race between Susan Collins and Troy Jackson is one of the nation's most high-profile Senate contests this year -- and may ultimately be decided by an especially powerful voting bloc: Maine women.

title: Another court blocks White House ballroom work, teeing up a Supreme Court review
description: A federal appeals court says above-ground construction cannot continue without approval from Congress, siding with historic preservation advocates.

title: Tariffs on brass instruments come too late for unemployed Ohio factory workers
description: The tariff proposal was announced three days after The Post's story on the shuttered factory.

title: Senate passes Russia sanctions bill that was long championed by Lindsey Graham
description: The bill is meant to stifle Russia's economy by allowing for tough new tariffs against major importers of Russian energy. The legislation was led by Lindsey Graham before his unexpected death in July.

title: Trump says he’d ‘probably get along’ with Jeffries as House speaker
description: Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-New York) is likely to lead the chamber if Democrats win it back.

title: The Senate wants a recess. Trump doesn’t.
description: Before senators leave for recess, Republican leaders are trying to plow through a lengthy to-do list.

title: In Texas, the economy rather than abortion takes center stage
description: Senate contenders James Talarico and Ken Paxton unveil dueling economic plans as this year’s campaigns turn from the culture wars that defined the state’s 2024 vote.
